note: Committed CI quality gates for the routing eval. Every threshold was derived from a measurement on this dataset, not chosen aspirationally. Regenerate the measurements with 'python -m evals.run --write-baseline' and re-review this file whenever evals/golden changes. Regeneration preserves the human-written sections below; it refreshes only `measurements` and `thresholds`, and re-marks a threshold `auto` if its value moved.
threshold_policy: threshold = floor(observed - 1.3 * standard_error), rounded down to two places. One standard error of a 379-case proportion is about 2.6 points, so a gate that sits exactly at the measurement fails the next case anyone relabels. 1.3 standard errors catches a real regression while tolerating the noise a set this size actually has. A threshold above the measurement is a permanent red build, which trains people to ignore the gate.
why_the_gate_is_low: The heuristic scores 0.533 on this dataset. The previous CI floor was 0.90 against an 18-case golden set the heuristic scored 18/18 on. That 100% was a property of the test set, not of the router: six of the eighteen cases are near-copies of the router's own regexes, and none of them exercised multi-turn input. The honest baseline is what is gated here. Raising the floor back to 0.90 would require either weakening the dataset or rewriting the router, and doing the first to pass the second is how an eval becomes theatre.

tfidf_logistic_regression.note: Measured with stratified group k-fold: near-duplicate cases are kept in one fold, so the out-of-fold score is not inflated by a twin of the test case sitting in training. Before that fix the same model scored 0.715 on a 379-case set and the gate was 0.68. The lower number is the honest one.

thresholds.name: min-accuracy
thresholds.rationale: Overall routing accuracy. 0.529 observed minus 1.3 SE (0.0251) is 0.497; rounded down to 0.49. Catches any change that costs more than about four percentage points.

thresholds.name: min-clear-accuracy
thresholds.rationale: Clear cases are where a transparent rule should work. 0.552 observed minus 1.3 SE (0.0299) is 0.514. If this stops being the strongest subset, the keyword scoring is no longer doing what it was written to do.

thresholds.name: min-ambiguous-accuracy
thresholds.rationale: Ambiguous cases carry a wide interval (0.384-0.565) because there are only 114 of them. 0.474 minus 1.3 SE (0.0465) is 0.413. Gated separately so a change that only hurts borderline input is caught even if the overall number moves little.

thresholds.name: min-adversarial-accuracy
thresholds.rationale: Adversarially tagged cases are the ones a real user could plausibly send. 0.474 minus 1.3 SE (0.0507) is 0.408. Smallest subset at 97 cases, so the floor is correspondingly loose; it exists to catch a collapse, not a two-point drift.

thresholds.name: min-accuracy
thresholds.rationale: Same policy applied to the learned baseline. 0.703 minus 1.3 SE (0.0224) is 0.674. Gated because the learned model is the reference implementation: if the heuristic is ever replaced by it, this floor has to hold too.

thresholds.name: min-ambiguous-accuracy
thresholds.rationale: 0.596 minus 1.3 SE (0.0450) is 0.538. This gate moved twice: from 0.57 when the 379-case set first moved it, and again when grouped folds removed a near-duplicate leak. Neither move was a dataset edit; both were measurement corrections.

deliberately_not_gated.reason: It evaluates 95 of 391 cases. A floor on it would be a floor on 25 ambiguous cases and 25 adversarial ones, where the interval is roughly plus or minus 17 points. Gating it would produce a build that flips on dataset edits without telling anyone anything about quality.
A floor reference, not a system anyone intends to ship. It is reported in results.json so the headline has something to be read against, and it is deliberately ungated.

The powerful tier sits at 0.250 for the heuristic with an interval of 0.174-0.349. A gate there would be inside its own noise. Per-tier numbers are reported on every run and the per-tier gate is available as --min-tier-accuracy for anyone who wants to raise one deliberately.

26 and 12 cases respectively. The heuristic scores 0.346 and 0.417 on them, which is a real and important finding, but one case is 4 points on the first subset and 8 on the second. Both are reported on every run and neither is gated until there are about 60 cases.
